title: Missing Number In Arithmetic Progression
statement: An arithmetic progression is a list in which every element exceeds the one before it by the same fixed amount (that amount may be negative or zero). The array `arr` was made from such a list by deleting exactly one element that was neither its first nor its last element. Return the deleted value. The input is guaranteed to have been built this way.
constraints: arr is an arithmetic progression with one inner element removed
notes:
## Intuition

The first and last elements were never removed, so they are the ends of the original progression, which had `n + 1` terms. The sum of an arithmetic progression depends only on its ends and its length: `(first + last) · (n + 1) / 2`. Subtract the sum of what is left and the difference is exactly the removed element. A brute-force alternative computes the step `(last - first) / n` and scans for the first element that is off; binary search on that same check also works in O(log n).

## Approach

1. Let `n` be the length of `arr`, and read `first` and `last`.
2. Compute `expectedSum`, the sum of the full progression of `n + 1` terms.
3. Add up the elements of `arr` into `actualSum`.
4. Return `expectedSum - actualSum`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [5, 7, 11, 13]`, so `n = 4`, `first = 5`, `last = 13`. The full progression has 5 terms, so `expectedSum = (5 + 13) · 5 / 2 = 45`. The loop gives `actualSum = 5 + 7 + 11 + 13 = 36`. The answer is `45 - 36 = 9`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to sum the array.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- The full progression has `n + 1` terms, not `n`; using `n` gives a wrong total.
- The step may be zero: every element is equal and the removed value equals them; the sum formula handles this, while dividing by the step would not.
- The step may be negative (a decreasing progression); do not assume the array increases.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of elements left in `arr` |
| `first`, `last` | the ends of the original progression |
| `expectedSum` | sum of the complete progression |
| `actualSum` | sum of the elements that remain |

narration.2: Count the elements that are left; the original progression had one more.
narration.3: The first element was never removed, so it starts the progression...
narration.5: Sum of the full progression: average of the ends times its n + 1 terms.
narration.6: Start adding up the elements that remain.
narration.8: Add it to the running total.
narration.10: Whatever the full sum has beyond the remaining sum is the removed element.
